feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital platform leadership and credible progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and scanability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression from coordinator to director, then consultant, which supports credibility and seniority.  
- Good use of scale and scope: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: combines strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a coherent way.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” and “content operations” appear frequently across summary, competencies, and roles. Tightening this would improve impact.  
- Improve structure and prioritization: there is overlap between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT. Consolidating these sections would make the CV cleaner and easier to scan.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage is uneven; capitalization is inconsistent in “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and relevant scope, but it’s slightly dense and repeats language already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it around outcomes and public-sector scale will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web ecosystems, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines enterprise website strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search to improve how mission-driven institutions publish, measure, and deliver information at scale.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, senior phrasing like “modernizing web ecosystems” or “leading enterprise digital platforms.”
- Add an outcome-oriented phrase such as “improve publishing efficiency, audience reach, and content discovery” if space allows.
- Keep tense/style consistent: “Leads” is fine, but a parallel structure across both sentences will read more smoothly.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search” is more specific and distinctive.
- “Complex, mission-driven organizations” is broad and somewhat repetitive with “public-sector communications.”
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased with sharper, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases and keep structure parallel; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “communications” inconsistently.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integration, and multimedia.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If targeting more technical roles, swap “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “CMS and digital platform delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector communications” and “AI-enabled… experiences” closely echo the header.
- Several items overlap heavily with Topline Skills; this section should stay broader, not tool-specific.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce the CV’s digital leadership theme, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and making the section more “selected projects” than a second experience summary would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, outcome-oriented line.
- Standardize style: use parallel verbs and consistent terms (e.g., “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” “main website” instead of “main site”).
- Add specificity where possible without repeating role bullets: note audience/problem solved rather than listing features.
- Suggested wording: “AI Hybrid Search: Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current and NACo role bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing similarly unique projects here.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it more outcome-led and tie it to 2–3 flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate bullets into impact areas: digital systems/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, governance/operations, AI search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, publishing speed, search relevance gains, stakeholder groups supported.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs like “led,” “built,” “implemented,” and “standardized.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats NACo and the summary; keep only what is new or more advanced here.
- AI-enabled search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects, so avoid restating the same details verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: for email/social/video/analytics/governance, include growth, efficiency, reporting cadence, production savings, engagement, or decision-making improvements if available.
- Condense softer phrasing: change “Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance...” to “Established publishing governance, editorial standards, and cross-department planning workflows to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, analytics, and studio buildout.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio rather than recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to execution-level leadership and channel growth, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening; use “managed” or “oversaw daily execution” instead.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling/standardizing here, not launching.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad, generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance  
- Editorial operations and publishing standards  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging  
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this skills block to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than listing generic capabilities.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases consistently and avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already well established in the header and NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, higher-value platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, impact-oriented summary: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here: remove jQuery, and consider removing WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages unless central to target roles.
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since recent experience is strongest there.
- Use parallel phrasing focused on capability, not just platforms: e.g., “Enterprise CMS modernization” instead of “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place unless it’s a signature differentiator.

Suggested edit:

- Tighten and group terms for flow: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” Technical + IT section almost exactly; use this section for strategic strengths and leave the full tools list below.
- “Leadership reporting” may be stronger as “executive reporting” or “executive dashboards.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or remove it if lightly used.
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want a stronger version: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web platforms) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Topline Skills entry listing the same platforms; keep one list broader and the other more selective.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list rather than a targeted capability statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” so it should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more current stack: “HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop “jQuery” unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place last or label as legacy support.
- Consider adding context in the heading or line label, e.g., “Front-End & Technical Implementation” to better match recent Drupal/CMS delivery work.
- If space allows, replace one tool with a stronger outcome-oriented capability: “CI/CD automation” instead of “GitHub Actions,” or “serverless scripting” instead of “Cloudflare Workers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.”
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under analytics/optimization unless you specifically use it for implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actively build with, and separate automation platforms from collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project/workflow management) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team coordination)**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general tools if space is tight; the strongest differentiators here are **Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.
- Airtable is already called out under Topline Skills (“Airtable systems”), so this section should stay concise rather than re-sell it.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The tools are relevant, especially given your recent email leadership at NACo, but this item is too bare to signal level of use or strategic scope. It would be stronger if framed as platforms you’ve operated for newsletter, member, and campaign communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (newsletter, campaign and member communications)**
- If accurate, add a proficiency cue tied to recent work: **Used to manage high-volume newsletter and advocacy email operations for member audiences**
- Keep only the 2–3 strongest/current platforms; list the one most central to your recent roles first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets already covering email/newsletter leadership; avoid repeating audience size or “tens of thousands” here
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless supported elsewhere; “member communications” is more specific and aligned with the CV

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, make it more specific and execution-oriented rather than repeating broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Google Tag Manager • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with the actual tools already listed; “dashboarding” is an output, not a technology.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal specialty instead of a generic term, e.g. **KPI reporting**, **conversion analysis**, or **event tracking architecture**.
- Keep only tools/methods you actively used in recent roles; prioritize GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, and Looker Studio given the NACo experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this section tools-only.
- **SEO** and **A/B testing** are capabilities, not platforms, so they may fit better in Topline Skills than Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, emphasizing team build-out, production ownership, and any scale/results you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to stress early-career scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs/results where possible: website refresh scope, livestream frequency/audience, weekly video cadence, email/social volume, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Example: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, streamline multi-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as foundational setup rather than enterprise leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the distinctive achievement and trim broad “supported programs and policy work” language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if possible: multimedia features, research briefs, web content, or stakeholder-facing materials.
- If you can, add scale or adoption: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced advocacy or member engagement.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression to digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills and multiple work bullets. Make it more tool-specific and current, emphasizing software proficiency rather than broad production capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software & Audio/Video Tools**
- Replace broad phrases with tool-led wording: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
